why_this_file_exists: This task's bound.md prints NO curvature-dependent illustrative figure for lane (b) (the count-unstated deployment modes), because no sourced M exists to plug into dbeta/beta ~ 0.29*sqrt((1-rho)*ln M / beta). This file exists anyway, as the completion gate and the handoff both require a companion f'' sensitivity table for 'any curvature-dependent figure', and serves here as the evidentiary basis for the bound.md decision to omit rather than illustrate: it shows that even at a FIXED, hypothetical M (i.e. holding the unsourced free parameter constant), the curvature-dependent readout itself already carries model-readout noise of the sizes tabulated below, from the BKZ-profile's own non-smoothness and from the linearisation-vs-finite-difference gap -- before any uncertainty in M is even introduced.

source.note: T3's task card frames its own linearisation-vs-finite-difference comparison as a DESIGN AUDIT, NOT A FINDING (obligation4_label_BINDING in T3's receipt.json), because the omitted/retained denominator ratio in dbeta = ln c / (2 ln delta) is 1/(4*beta*ln delta), fixed a priori and derivable before running anything. fpp_sensitivity_table.description: Three independent, already-measured indicators of how much a curvature-dependent (f''-dependent) dbeta/beta or core-SVP-bit readout moves, at these three FIXED baseline betas, purely from properties of the cost model and its optimiser -- with M (hence ln M) held out of the picture entirely, since these are all fixed-M / fixed-c comparisons.

indicator_1_beta_integer_staircase_non_m.what: beta*(c), the estimator's own optimised block size as a function of the norm-scaling knob c, is integer-valued and NOT non-decreasing in c -- i.e. it can go the WRONG WAY as the scaled quantity grows, purely from the optimiser's discrete search.
indicator_1_beta_integer_staircase_non_m.magnitude: up to 2 blocks per anomalous pair, e.g. Kyber512 c = 0.9775 -> 0.98 gives beta 387 -> 389 while 0.98 -> 0.9825 gives 389 -> 387
indicator_1_beta_integer_staircase_non_m.consequence_for_a_curvature_dependent_fi: at the finer end of the scan (c = 0.99, 0.98) the finite-difference dbeta signal is 0 to 6 blocks, i.e. comparable in size to this optimiser scatter; a single-cell curvature readout at that resolution cannot be distinguished from integer selection noise

indicator_2_linearisation_vs_finite_diff.what: OLS slope of beta on ln(c) over the 41 scanned points, compared against the linearised closed form 1/(2 ln delta) that a fixed-curvature approximation would use
indicator_2_linearisation_vs_finite_diff.consequence_for_a_curvature_dependent_fi: the three ratios do not share a sign (Kyber512/768 read low, Kyber1024 reads high), so no single correction factor can be applied uniformly across FIPS 203 parameter sets; a dbeta/beta readout using a fixed-curvature (linearised) approximation is off by roughly -4% to +3% relative to the estimator's own finite-difference behaviour at these baselines

indicator_3_omitted_over_retained_denomi.what: 1/(4*beta*ln delta), the ratio of the term a fixed-d, fixed-m linearisation of dbeta = ln c / (2 ln delta) drops to the term it keeps. Fixed a priori by the formula alone -- NOT measured, NOT fitted -- and reused here only as a curvature-sensitivity RANGE, per T3's own DESIGN AUDIT, NOT A FINDING label, which this file preserves.
indicator_3_omitted_over_retained_denomi.range_pct: 12.7% to 15.9% across the three FIPS 203 baselines
indicator_3_omitted_over_retained_denomi.consequence_for_a_curvature_dependent_fi: a linearised dbeta/beta figure omits a term worth 12.7-15.9% of the retained term at these betas, purely as a property of the formula's own algebra, independent of any measurement
indicator_3_omitted_over_retained_denomi.reused_verbatim_from: TASK-20260805-9672b3/receipt.json headline_observations_NO_INTERPRETATION.6_toy_shapes.a_priori_ratio_DESIGN_AUDIT (labelled DESIGN AUDIT there; label preserved here)

indicator_4_bits_per_block_constant_mism.what: the card's own conversion constant 0.292 (classical core-sieve exponent) compared against the estimator's own OLS-measured bits-per-block over the same scanned range under RC.MATZOV
indicator_4_bits_per_block_constant_mism.consequence_for_a_curvature_dependent_fi: converting a block-count delta into a bit figure using the fixed 0.292 constant, rather than RC.MATZOV's own measured slope, overstates the bit figure by roughly 4.1% to 6.5% at these baselines -- two DIFFERENT models (0.292 classical core-sieve vs RC.MATZOV), not a measurement-vs-truth comparison

how_this_bears_on_lane_b_of_bound.md: If bound.md had instead chosen to print an illustrative G-bits figure for lane (b) at some stipulated M, that figure would need to carry this table beside it per the handoff and the completion gate. The table shows the underlying dbeta/beta or core-SVP-bit readout is ALREADY unstable by single-digit-to-teens percent, or by up to 2 integer blocks, at FIXED M -- before layering an entirely unsourced M on top. bound.md's decision to omit the illustrative figure rather than present one number as if it were precise is made with this table as its explicit basis.
explicitly_not_transported: None of these numbers is transported to a claim about ML-KEM's real-world security margin. TASK-20260805-9672b3's own baselines (beta 389/606/855, d 1005/1420/1867) ARE the crypto-scale Kyber512/768/1024 shapes -- unlike T2's toy-scale (d<=140, beta<=40) measurements elsewhere in this goal -- but nothing here is subtracted from the in-repo primal_bdd margins of 2.80/6.04/1.28 bits, and no attack, break, or security claim in either direction is made.
